scam.title: Protect yourself from scams
scam.lead: People run scams in the name of the lottery. Know the official fee and check every step yourself.
scam.banner: Registering for the lottery has an official fee of just one dollar ($1), set by the US State Department. Any extra money is the office's service charge.

facts.1: You can register yourself on the official site that the US State Department announces.
facts.2: If you use an office, make sure it registers on the official site only, and that you personally keep the confirmation number.
facts.3: Nobody can guarantee a win or raise your chances.
facts.4: You check the result yourself, only on the official Entrant Status Check. No email or message tells you that you won.
facts.5: Copycat sites look official. Make sure the address ends in .gov, and beware of anyone who asks for money to "win".

signs.1: Asks for money to "guarantee" a win or raise your chances.
signs.2: Tells you that you won by message, email or phone.
signs.3: Asks for a money transfer, card details or your passport before you check the official site.
signs.4: The address does not end in .gov, or the tone is urgent and threatening.

guide.title: How do I find the price of food?
guide.lead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to see it yourself, in the city you plan to live in.
guide.step1: Open a supermarket site from the links below and pick a store in your intended city.
guide.step2: Build a one-week basket of what you actually buy and read the total.
guide.step3: Multiply by 4 and type the number into the calculator. Repeat now and then; prices change.
guide.note: These are external sites. We do not set prices and are not responsible for them.
guide.backToCalculator: Type the number into the calculator
guide.titleFor: How do I find the price of “{item}”?
guide.genericLead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to look, and you type the number into the calculator.
guide.genericStep1: Open the links below and look for the current fee or price.
guide.genericStep2: Type the number as you find it. Mind the currency, and whether it is one-off or monthly.
guide.genericStep3: Go back to the calculator and type the number. Check it now and then; prices and fees change.

guideHealth.title: How do I find the price of health insurance?
guideHealth.lead: We will not give you a number. The price depends on the state, your age, household size and income, and you see it yourself on the official US government site.
guideHealth.step1: Open HealthCare.gov, enter the ZIP code of your intended city, and your household members and ages.
guideHealth.step2: Browse the plans and the monthly premium of each one, and check whether a subsidy applies to your expected income.
guideHealth.step3: Type the monthly premium into the calculator. If you have children, include them in the household size so the premium covers them.
guideHealth.state: Some states run their own marketplace; HealthCare.gov sends you there automatically. We do not set prices.
